target_customer: Software companies and developers who need usage metering and usage-based billing for APIs and AI products
problem: Companies that bill by usage must collect and aggregate billions of events accurately and in real time; most build this in-house.
business_model: Open source core (Apache 2.0) plus paid managed cloud and enterprise plans
product_category: Developer infrastructure: usage metering and billing

founders.name: Peter Marton
founders.background_notes: Worked on Stripe's usage and cost platform per YC page.

founders.name: Andras Toth
founders.background_notes: Worked on Backyards (Calisti) at Banzai Cloud, acquired by Cisco.

technical_complexity.rationale: Accurate real-time aggregation of billions of events needed Kafka and an analytics store (ClickHouse), exactly-once style correctness and billing integrations.

defensibility.rationale: Open source lowers the moat but builds adoption; billing integrations create lock-in once deployed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Stripe offered usage billing and later acquired Metronome according to 2026 comparison articles; Kong acquired OpenMeter in September 2025.

market_need_then: AI and API products were moving to usage-based pricing and founders said metering needed standardization. No dated 2023 source was read for spend or complaints.

branding.name_origin: Open (open source) plus meter (usage metering); inferred from the product description, no source states the naming story.

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer-first, open source advocacy; blog post why billing must be open source

rebrands.why: Folded into Kong Konnect after acquisition

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt listing with about 670 followers; GitHub star count not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear descriptive name and open source credibility, but modest community evidence.

outcome_analysis: OpenMeter raised a $3M seed in March 2024 and was acquired by Kong on September 3, 2025, with the founders and team joining Kong and the project staying open source. Founder experience with Stripe usage billing and the rise of AI usage pricing fit the timing. The price was not disclosed, so whether it was a strong outcome for investors is unknown.
notes: Seed seen in TechCrunch URL (March 2024), SaaS News and aggregators, all agreeing on $3M and investors; I did not fetch the TechCrunch article body, so the amount rests on search summaries. CB Insights says $3.5M over 3 rounds, unexplained. Acquisition price undisclosed. Competitor search returned only post-2024 vendor blogs (Lago, Orb, Metronome, Amberflo), nothing dated near early 2023, so the list is empty. Later events: Metronome acquired by Stripe and Orb by Adyen per 2026 articles, unverified.
